inline.s: [Broad and long tongue] One of the Buddha’s thirty-two marks: the Buddha’s tongue is broad and long, soft, red, and thin, able to cover the face up to the hairline. With such a tongue, his speech is necessarily true. [Covering the whole three-thousand great-thousand world, speaking words of truth] To the whole three-thousand great-thousand world that he teaches, he speaks words of truth. [Three-thousand great-thousand world] That is, a great-thousand world, which is the region that a single Buddha teaches. One Mount Sumeru together with the four great continents is called a small world. A collection of one thousand small worlds is called a “small-thousand world”; a collection of one thousand small-thousand worlds is called a “middle-thousand world”; a collection of one thousand middle-thousand worlds is called a “great-thousand world.” Because it reckons by thousands three times, a great-thousand world is also called a “three-thousand great-thousand world.” [A sūtra protected and recollected by all Buddhas] This Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Amitābha Buddha is protected and recollected by all Buddhas. The passage below explains:

“Why is it called the sūtra protected and recollected by all Buddhas? Sāriputra! If virtuous men or virtuous women hear this sūtra and uphold it, and hear the names of all the Buddhas, these virtuous men and women are all protected and recollected by all the Buddhas, and all attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.”

[Sāriputra! In the southern world there are the Buddha Sun-Moon-Lamp, the Buddha Renowned Light, the Buddha Great-Blaze-Shoulder, the Buddha Sumeru-Lamp, the Buddha Immeasurable Diligence, and so on, Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Each in his own land puts forth the broad and long tongue, covering the whole three-thousand great-thousand world, and speaks words of truth: “You sentient beings should believe in this sūtra that praises the inconceivable merit and virtue and is protected and recollected by all Buddhas.”]

Sāriputra! In the southern world there are the Buddha Sun-Moon-Lamp, the Buddha Renowned Light, the Buddha Great-Blaze-Shoulder, the Buddha Sumeru-Lamp, the Buddha Immeasurable Diligence, and so on, Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. [Sāriputra! In the western world there are the Buddha Immeasurable Life, the Buddha Immeasurable Marks, the Buddha Immeasurable Banner

[Sāriputra! In the world below there are the Buddha Lion, the Buddha Renowned, the Buddha Renowned-Light, the Buddha Dharma, the Buddha Dharma-Banner, the Buddha Upholding-Dharma, and so on, Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Each in his own land puts forth the broad and long tongue, covering the whole three-thousand great-thousand world, and speaks words of truth: “You sentient beings should believe in this sūtra that praises the inconceivable merit and virtue and is protected and recollected by all Buddhas.”]

[Sāriputra! In the world above there are the Buddha Brahma-Sound, the Buddha Star-King, the Buddha Supreme-Fragrance, the Buddha Fragrance-Light, the Buddha Great-Blaze-Shoulder, the Buddha Adorned with Assorted Jewelled Flowers, the Buddha King of the Sal Trees, the Buddha Jewelled Flower Virtue, the Buddha Who Sees the Meaning of All Things, the Buddha Like Mount Sumeru, and so on, Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Each in his own land puts forth the broad and long tongue, covering the whole three-thousand great-thousand world, and speaks words of truth: “You sentient beings should believe in this sūtra that praises the inconceivable merit and virtue and is protected and recollected by all Buddhas.”]

Sāriputra! In the world above there are the Buddha Brahma-Sound, the Buddha Star-King, the Buddha Supreme-Fragrance, the Buddha Fragrance-Light, the Buddha Great-Blaze-Shoulder, the Buddha Adorned with Assorted Jewelled Flowers, the Buddha King of the Sal Trees, the Buddha Jewelled Flower Virtue, the Buddha Who Sees the Meaning of All Things, the Buddha Like Mount Sumeru, and so on, Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Each in his own land puts forth the broad and long tongue, and to the whole three-thousand great-thousand world that he teaches speaks words of truth: You sentient beings should all believe in and accept this sūtra that praises the inconceivable merit and virtue of Amitābha Buddha and is protected and recollected by all Buddhas.

[Sāriputra! What do you think? Why is it called the sūtra protected and recollected by all Buddhas? Sāriputra! If virtuous men or virtuous women hear this sūtra and uphold it, and hear the names of all the Buddhas, these virtuous men and virtuous women are all protected and recollected by all the Buddhas, and all attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.]

Sāriputra! What do you think? Why is this sūtra called the sūtra protected and recollected by all Buddhas? Sāriputra! If virtuous men or virtuous women hear this sūtra and believe in and accept it, and practice in accordance with it, and also hear the names of all the Buddhas, these virtuous men and women are all protected and recollected by all the Buddhas, and no longer retrogress from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi (the stage of Buddhahood).

[One who hears this sūtra and upholds it] “Receive” means to believe and accept; “uphold” means to act in accordance with the scripture. “One who hears this sūtra and upholds it” is one who believes in and accepts this sūtra and practices in accordance with it. [The Chinese transliteration a-nou (
nòu
)-duo-luo-san-miao (
miǎo

)-san-puti] Sanskrit transliteration. Translated into Chinese it means: the supreme, correct, and equal enlightenment. An arhat attains correct enlightenment; a bodhisattva attains correct and equal enlightenment; a Buddha attains the supreme, correct, and equal enlightenment.
The Tang translation says:

“Sāriputra, if virtuous men or virtuous women have already heard, or will hear, or now hear this sūtra and, having heard it, deeply give rise to faith and understanding. Having given rise to faith and understanding, they must surely be received and taken in by the World-Honored Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges rivers, dwelling in the ten directions.
Those who practice as taught
, all are certain to be non-retrogressing from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and all are certain to be reborn in the pure Buddha land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Immeasurable Life Buddha.”
[Jingjia (
jìng jiā

)] A Sanskrit transliteration of “Ganges.” [Those who practice as taught: all are certain to be non-retrogressing from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi] Those who practice as taught are all certain never to retrogress, advancing from the higher to the highest, until they attain Buddhahood.
[Therefore, Sāriputra! You should all believe in and accept my words, and what the Buddhas have said.]
Therefore, Sāriputra! You should all believe in and accept what I have said and what the Buddhas above have said; practice as taught, and harbor no doubt.
The Tang translation says:
“Therefore, Sāriputra, you sentient beings should all believe in, accept, and understand the words of me and of the World-Honored Buddhas of the ten directions; diligently and earnestly
practice as taught, and harbor no doubt

[Sāriputra! If there are people who have made the vow, who now make the vow, or who will make the vow, desiring to be reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha, these people all attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi in that land — whether they have already been reborn, are now reborn, or will be reborn.]

Sāriputra! If there are people who have already made the vow, now make the vow, or will make the vow (establishing the vow to hold fast to the name and attain single-mindedness without confusion), desiring to be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, they are all certainly able to go, and there, without retrogressing, practice to Buddhahood — whether they have already been reborn, are now reborn, or will be reborn.
[Making the vow] Establishing a vow.
The Tang translation says:

“Sāriputra, if virtuous men or virtuous women, regarding the merit, virtue, and adornment of the pure Buddha land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Immeasurable Life, have already made the vow, will make the vow, or now make the vow, they must surely be received and taken in by the World-Honored Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges rivers, dwelling in the ten directions.
Those who practice as taught
, all are certain to be non-retrogressing from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and all are certain to be reborn in the pure Buddha land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Immeasurable Life Buddha.”
[Therefore, Sāriputra! If virtuous men and virtuous women have faith, they should make the vow, that they may be reborn in that land.]
Therefore, Sāriputra! If virtuous men and virtuous women have faith, they should make the vow to be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Tang translation says:

“Therefore, Sāriputra, if virtuous men or virtuous women of pure faith, all should, regarding the pure Buddha land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Immeasurable Life, with deep mind believe and understand, make the vow and be reborn,
and not practice laxity
[Do not practice laxity] Never give oneself up to indulgent ease; diligently and without slack, practice as taught.

[Sāriputra! As I now praise the inconceivable merit and virtue of the Buddhas, those Buddhas in turn praise my inconceivable merit and virtue, saying: Śākyamuni Buddha is able to do an exceedingly difficult and rare thing! In the Sahā land, in the evil world of the five turbidities (the turbidity of the eon, the turbidity of views, the turbidity of afflictions, the turbidity of sentient beings, and the turbidity of life), he attains anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and for the sake of sentient beings speaks this Dharma that is hard to believe in all the world.]

Sāriputra! As I now praise the inconceivable merit and virtue of the Buddhas, those Buddhas in turn praise my inconceivable merit and virtue, saying: Śākyamuni Buddha is able to do an exceedingly difficult and rare thing! In the evil world of the five turbidities (the turbidity of the eon, the turbidity of views, the turbidity of afflictions, the turbidity of sentient beings, and the turbidity of life) of the Sahā land, he realizes Buddhahood, and for the sake of sentient beings speaks this Dharma that is hard to believe in all the world.
[Sahā (
suō

)-land] “Sahā” is Sanskrit transliteration. Translated into Chinese it means “Capable of Enduring” (kanren). It means that the sentient beings of this land are content in the ten evils, endure the three poisons and all afflictions, and are unwilling to leave and get out; hence it is called the World of Endurance (the Sahā world), or in short the Land of Endurance. [The turbidity of the eon, the turbidity of views, the turbidity of afflictions, the turbidity of sentient beings, and the turbidity of life] The turbidity of the eon: born in a degenerate age, war, famine, plague and the like arise one after another, the people suffer unspeakably, and there is never a day of peace. The turbidity of views: people’s views are not correct, they do not revere the true Way, and diverse teachings abound, with no one reaching agreement. The turbidity of afflictions: people are greedy for love and pleasure, wrathful and contentious, endlessly false and deceitful. The turbidity of sentient beings: people are for the most part corrupt and evil, body and mind impure, and fail to grasp principle. The turbidity of life: because afflictions gather thickly, body and mind are worn out, and life is short. [The Dharma hard to believe] The Land of Ultimate Bliss is so supreme that, once one attains single-mindedness without confusion, one can rely on the Buddha’s power and be reborn there, attaining Buddhahood in a single lifetime. But how many people in the world truly believe and practice as taught? Therefore this is a Dharma hard to believe in the world.

[Sāriputra! Know that I, in the evil world of the five turbidities, did this difficult thing — attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi and spoke this hard-to-believe Dharma for all the world — this is exceedingly difficult!]

Sāriputra! You should know that I, in the evil world of the five turbidities, did this difficult thing — realized Buddhahood and spoke this hard-to-believe Dharma for all the world — this is truly exceedingly difficult!

[When the Buddha had spoken this sūtra, Sāriputra and the monks, all the devas, humans, asuras and others of the world, having heard what the Buddha said, joyfully believed and accepted it, and made obeisance and departed.]

When the Buddha had proclaimed this sūtra, Sāriputra and the monks, all the devas, humans, asuras and others of the world, having heard what the Buddha said, joyfully believed and accepted it, and made obeisance and departed.

[Deva] One of the six destinies, the one with the most excellent retribution among the six, with a very long lifespan and a life of felicity. [Six destinies] Hells, hungry ghosts, animals, asuras, humans, and devas. [Asura] One of the six destinies; translated into Chinese it means “not a deva,” because they have the bliss of devas and humans but not their virtue — like devas, yet not devas. In their former lives they too were quite willing to cultivate merit, but their envy and hatred were very heavy, and so they turned and were reborn in the asura destiny. [Samsara] Sentient beings, from the beginningless past, transmigrate through birth and death within the six destinies, turning like a wheel without cease.
